design_summary.purpose: adaptive_aero_control_top is a synthesizable FPGA transport-and-guard controller for an automotive active-aerodynamics use case. It does not implement the DoMINO surrogate model locally; instead it packages outbound model requests, accepts and validates inbound responses from an external GPU-hosted service, enforces freshness and protocol correctness, clamps actuator commands to programmed limits, and falls back to a deterministic safe command whenever configuration, timing, or protocol conditions are invalid.
design_summary.operating_model: The design runs in one clock domain with clk and active-low rst_n. Software configures the controller through a small register window. When enabled and configuration is valid, the transport FSM issues at most one outstanding request at a time, holds req_valid until handshake or cancellation, and embeds transaction ID plus compact request metadata into req_data. The inbound response stream is consumed only when resp_valid and resp_ready handshake, and responses are accepted only if the transaction ID matches the outstanding request and the freshness timeout has not expired. Valid command summaries are then clamped into the actuator window and emitted on act_cmd_valid/act_cmd_data. Any reset, disable, timeout, malformed response, mismatch, invalid configuration, or protocol error forces safe fallback behavior.

external_interfaces.purpose: Outbound DoMINO model request packaging and backpressure handling.
Inbound response acceptance and validation from the external GPU-hosted service.
Scalar configuration, control, and status readback.
Bounded actuator command emission with deterministic fallback support.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Top-level synthesizable FPGA controller and sole integration point for the active-aerodynamics request/response contract.
responsibilities: Provide the sole top-level integration point for request/response streaming, register access, and actuator command emission.
Maintain one outstanding transaction ID and monotonically increment it for each new request issuance.
Encode compact model request packets with transaction ID, velocity setpoint, geometry source flags, and format selector flags.
Monitor freshness timeout from request issuance and expire the outstanding request when the configured limit is exceeded.
Validate response transaction ID, response-valid flag, and freshness before accepting command summary fields.
Clamp actuator commands to configured min/max bounds and mark clamp-applied status when saturation occurs.
Force deterministic safe fallback command on reset, timeout, disable, invalid configuration, malformed response, or protocol error.
Continue accepting register writes during fallback and permit recovery only after configuration becomes valid and a new request can be issued.
interface_notes: External ports are fixed to clk, rst_n, req_valid, req_ready, req_data, resp_valid, resp_ready, resp_data, reg_we, reg_re, reg_addr, reg_wdata, reg_rdata, act_cmd_valid, and act_cmd_data.
The top must not expose bulk vehicle geometry, mesh data, pressure fields, or flow fields as pins.
req_valid is owned by the transport logic and remains asserted until handshake or cancellation.
resp_ready is owned by the transport logic and is asserted only when an outstanding response can be consumed.
reg_rdata is owned by the MMIO logic and returns readable configuration and status information.
act_cmd_valid/act_cmd_data are driven by the transport logic after validation or fallback selection.
ownership_notes: signal ownership remains with the named internal submodules as specified.
No additional hierarchy, modules, or ports are introduced.
Filename association is inherited from the spec as adaptive_aero_control_top.v.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top_mmio
module_architecture.role: Internal MMIO/register and control-sequencing wrapper that decodes the register window, stores scalar configuration/state/status registers, generates semantic control outputs, and returns readable register data.
responsibilities: Accept external writes to enable, mode, velocity setpoint, freshness timeout, actuator min/max, safe fallback command, transaction ID seed, geometry format selector, and reference-geometry enable flag.
Provide readback of configuration, status, and last transaction ID fields through reg_rdata.
Generate explicit semantic configuration outputs used by the transport controller.
Expose config_valid based on programmed scalar register consistency, including actuator_min <= actuator_max and valid enable/configuration combinations.
Retain register contents across cycles and update only on reg_we transactions.
Supply register-derived status readback without requiring any bulk storage of model data.
interface_notes: The module is internal to the top-level contract and is not a separate top-level endpoint.
It receives clk, rst_n, reg_we, reg_re, reg_addr, and reg_wdata, and drives reg_rdata plus semantic configuration outputs.
It consumes status inputs from the transport controller and maps them into readable status fields.
It does not store bulk geometry, mesh, or flow payloads in flip-flop arrays; only scalar control fields and status bookkeeping are retained.
Geometry metadata is limited to compact descriptors/flags: geometry format selector and reference-geometry source enable.
ownership_notes: reg_rdata is driven by this module.

cfg_enable, cfg_mode, cfg_velocity_setpoint, cfg_freshness_timeout, cfg_actuator_min, cfg_actuator_max, cfg_safe_fallback_cmd, cfg_tx_id_seed, cfg_geometry_format, cfg_ref_geometry_enable, and config_valid are driven by this module.
Status inputs are owned by the transport block and only read here for status reporting.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top_transport
module_architecture.role: Internal request/response FSM and actuator-command enforcement block for request issuance, response validation, timeout management, and safe fallback sequencing.
responsibilities: Assemble outbound req_data with transaction ID, velocity setpoint, geometry reference metadata, geometry format selector, and control flags for DrivAerML reference geometry and STL format.
Assert req_valid until req_ready handshake occurs or request is canceled by reset or disable.
Assert resp_ready only when expecting a response and able to consume resp_data on handshake.
Reject mismatched, stale, malformed, or invalid-status responses and set protocol-error or stale-rejected status accordingly.
Maintain a freshness counter started at request issuance and expire the request at the configured timeout.
Force safe fallback command on reset, disable, timeout, invalid configuration, or protocol error.
Clamp all outgoing commands to the actuator min/max range when configuration is valid.
Drive status outputs for busy, request outstanding, response accepted, stale response rejected, clamp applied, fallback active, protocol error, and last transaction IDs.
interface_notes: The module receives all semantic configuration from MMIO and sends all status back to MMIO.
It directly owns the outbound and inbound streaming handshake behavior.
It is responsible for the 128-bit request packet layout and 128-bit response parsing contract.
It uses a 32-bit actuator command path, a small freshness timer, and a compact transaction ID counter.
It must not drive any MMIO configuration inputs or external backpressure/response inputs.
Response acceptance is strictly handshake-based using resp_valid and resp_ready.
ownership_notes: req_valid, req_data, resp_ready, act_cmd_valid, act_cmd_data, status_busy, status_req_outstanding, status_resp_accepted, status_stale_resp_rejected, status_clamp_applied, status_fallback_active, status_protocol_error, status_last_accepted_txid, and status_last_rejected_txid are driven by this module.
All configuration inputs are received from MMIO and are not driven here.

interface_summary.intent: Provide a small scalar register window for configuration, control, and readable status.
Transport outbound model requests and inbound model responses using a compact valid/ready streaming protocol.
Emit bounded actuator commands only after validation or via deterministic safe fallback.
Provide scalar configuration and configuration-validity indication for request generation, freshness monitoring, and clamping.
Return readable transport and safety status plus transaction tracking information to the register block.

data_flow_summary: Configuration writes enter adaptive_aero_control_top_mmio, which stores only scalar registers and compact geometry descriptors/flags, then publishes semantic configuration outputs.

When cfg_enable is asserted and config_valid is true, adaptive_aero_control_top_transport issues at most one outstanding request, increments the transaction ID monotonically, and packages request metadata into req_data.
req_valid remains asserted until req_ready acknowledges the request or the request is canceled by reset or disable.
Inbound resp_data is only consumed on resp_valid and resp_ready handshake, and the embedded transaction ID must match the latest outstanding request.
Freshness timing begins at request issuance and expires according to cfg_freshness_timeout; late responses are rejected and fallback is asserted.
Valid response command summaries are clamped to cfg_actuator_min/cfg_actuator_max before act_cmd_data is emitted.
If configuration is invalid, including cfg_actuator_min > cfg_actuator_max, the block remains in safe fallback until corrected.
Status bits and last accepted/rejected transaction IDs are carried from the transport FSM back into the MMIO block for readable register access.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: The design uses a single synchronous clock domain driven by clk. All internal control, status, counter, and handshake state is updated synchronously on clk.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: rst_n is active-low. During reset assertion, all outputs are deasserted, request state is cleared, freshness and transaction tracking are cleared, and the controller enters deterministic safe fallback behavior. After reset release, fallback remains active until a valid enable and valid configuration are present and a new request can be issued.

integration_notes: The top-level I/O count is kept compact by exposing only streaming transport, scalar register access, and a single actuator command channel; no geometry arrays, mesh data, pressure fields, or flow fields appear as pins.
The register window is minimal and scalar-only; geometry-related information is intentionally reduced to compact metadata fields rather than bulk storage.

The FPGA memory contract is descriptive only: any bulk payload, history, or FIFO storage needed by implementation flow must be mapped through a technology-neutral memory wrapper to native block RAM, not flattened into registers.
The design is synthesizable RTL only and relies on FSMs, counters, comparators, register file logic, handshake logic, and saturation logic.
No ASIC hard macro is instantiated in the FPGA prototype.
Recovery from fallback is allowed only after configuration is valid and a new request can be presented under the enabled state.

Status reporting includes busy, request outstanding, response accepted, stale response rejected, clamp applied, fallback active, protocol error, and last accepted/rejected transaction IDs, all via the MMIO read path.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
